clue.text: 'Tigers let loose in county town'? One can't get lower than this (13, two words)

definitions.text: One can't get lower than this

indicators.note: animals let loose scatter in no fixed order, so the letters of the big cats are scrambled
the scrambled letters are placed inside the town named next

blocks.note: taken as written, then scrambled
Chester is the county town of Cheshire

explanation.surface: A headline about tigers escaping in a county town, followed by a remark about something at rock bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted phrase is the wordplay; the second sentence is the definition. Chester is the county town of Cheshire in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The chest register is the lowest range of the singing voice, so a singer cannot go deeper than it.

clue.text: Type of granule in e.g. algae disheartened pupil in art school dreadfully

definitions.text: Type of granule in e.g. algae

indicators.note: losing its heart means everything between the ends goes, leaving the outer letters
done dreadfully, the letters come out in a mess
the short piece sits inside the jumbled letters

blocks.note: outer letters of the word
taken as written, then scrambled

explanation.surface: A dispirited student struggling with biology of algae at art college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupil' is not L for learner here: losing its heart keeps just its two end letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A chloroplast is the chlorophyll-holding body in plant and algal cells, a granule-like structure where photosynthesis happens.

clue.text: African lingo almost takes over western nation

indicators.note: almost all of the word means its last letter is dropped
in a down entry one part sits over, so above, the other

blocks.note: to have is to take
the United States is a western nation

explanation.surface: An African language nearly conquers a Western country.
explanation.definitionFit: Hausa is a major language of northern Nigeria and Niger, spoken across West Africa.

clue.text: Singular heron seizes one with raised wings?

indicators.note: to seize something is to hold it within one's grasp

blocks.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
an egret is a kind of heron
an means one

explanation.surface: An odd heron catches a bird that has its wings up.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags heraldry: the answer is a term for a winged beast in a coat of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry segreant describes a griffin rampant with wings raised and spread.

clue.text: Criminal gang brought to court, one not English

indicators.note: one letter stands in place of another that is no longer there

blocks.note: a defendant brought to court is tried
a means one
E abbreviates English

explanation.surface: A gang of criminals is prosecuted, with one member who is not English.
explanation.definitionFit: Triads are Chinese organised-crime syndicates, so a triad is a criminal gang.

clue.text: King lives — Henry kept in for rupture

indicators.note: something kept in is held inside another

blocks.note: Rex is Latin for king
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
is, as in exists or lives

explanation.surface: A king survives while Henry is locked up, causing a split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry' looks like a royal name to match 'King', but it is the unit of inductance.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhexis is a medical term for the bursting or rupture of a blood vessel or organ.

clue.text: Hearts sinking after overthrow of celebrated champ

indicators.note: overthrowing turns a thing upside down, which in a down entry reads it backwards
the letter sinks below, so comes after the other part in a down entry

blocks.note: to celebrate in song is to sing, past tense sang
H is the card abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: Fans' spirits fall after a celebrated champion is toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champ' is not a champion but the verb to bite noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ is to bite or grind the teeth, which is what gnashing means.

clue.text: Fibrous stuff extractable from mistletoe

indicators.note: it can be drawn straight out of the next word's letters

blocks.note: letters two to six of the word

explanation.surface: Fibre that can be extracted from the mistletoe plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a strong fibre from Mexican agave and yucca plants, used for cord and brushes.

clue.text: Gin time — lubricant follows

indicators.note: the second item comes after the first in the written order

blocks.note: T abbreviates time
oil is a lubricant

explanation.surface: It's time for gin, then something to grease the wheels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' is the trap, not the spirit; toil in the old sense of a net or snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a snare for game, and toils are nets or traps, as in caught in the toils.

clue.text: Modesty at being separated from clothes, blushing all round?

indicators.note: separating two letters from the word means they are taken off
one word goes all the way round the other

blocks.note: taken as written; these letters are removed
attire means clothing
a blush is a reddening of the face

explanation.surface: A shy person blushes all over at being stripped of their clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blushing' reads as an adjective but stands for the noun REDNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiredness means a retiring, reserved nature, so it is a synonym of modesty.

clue.text: Dither before deciding to take queen

blocks.note: to have is to take, as in having a biscuit
R for Regina, queen

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates before choosing whether to capture the queen, as in chess.
explanation.definitionFit: To haver is a Scots word for vacillating or hesitating, which is what dithering before a decision means.

clue.text: Composer of memorial the piper played round centre of grave

indicators.note: something played is performed with freedom, so the letters are rearranged
the middle letter of the next word is the one used
the rearranged letters go round the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written, then scrambled
middle letter of the five-letter word

explanation.surface: A piper plays a lament at a graveside, and someone writes the tribute.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitapher writes epitaphs, the inscriptions or verses commemorating the dead on a memorial.

clue.text: Student endlessly studying eastern China

blocks.note: a spod is a dull swot, a student forever at their books
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: A student who never stops studying eastern China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' is not cutting a word here: the whole phrase describes a spod, a swot. 'China' with its capital hidden at the start is the porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Spode is a famous make of English porcelain, and china is the general word for such porcelain.

clue.text: Cook aching to become No. 1 in his profession?

blocks.note: to do food is to cook it
a yen is a longing or ache

explanation.surface: A cook longs to rise to the top of the culinary profession.
explanation.definitionFit: The doyen is the senior or most respected member of a group, its leading figure.

clue.text: Jock's dish, one replacing silver in cases etc

indicators.note: one item takes the place of another inside the word for travel bags

blocks.note: suitcases and the like are luggage
Roman numeral one
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's dish, with one item swapped for silver among the cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jock' is a nickname for a Scot, marking a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: A luggie is a Scots wooden bowl with lug-like handles, a kind of dish.

clue.text: Loyalist Irishman leading civil disobedience

indicators.note: the first item goes in front of the second, as a leader goes ahead

blocks.note: Pat is a stock name for an Irishman
a riot is a violent public disturbance

explanation.surface: A Loyalist Irishman at the head of a campaign of civil disobedience.
explanation.walkthrough: In Northern Ireland a Loyalist is a political label, which makes the Irish surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot is someone loyal to their country, so the word means a loyalist.

clue.text: Prince heading alliance accepted way of doing things

indicators.note: one part stands at the head of the other, so it is written first

blocks.note: Pr is a dictionary abbreviation for prince
an axis is an alliance of states, as in the wartime Axis

explanation.surface: A prince leads an alliance that has adopted a set procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: Praxis is established practice or custom, the usual accepted manner of doing something.

clue.text: What's one in Mobil at, deviously making a packet?

indicators.note: the item is placed inside the following words
a devious route twists about, so the letters wander out of order

blocks.note: a means one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone at the oil company Mobil is making a fortune by dishonest means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A packet' looks like a large sum of money, but it is a packet boat, a ship carrying mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A packet was a ship running a regular service carrying mail and passengers, the same thing as a mail boat.

clue.text: Level pay increase, by the sound of it (to do with limiting extremes?)

indicators.note: we are told to go by how the phrase is spoken, not how it is written

blocks.note: a pay increase is a raise, which is pronounced the same as the target

explanation.surface: A flat pay rise for everyone, which is said to narrow the gap between top and bottom earners.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed aside is a playful extra: the answer sets A and Z, the extremes of the alphabet, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To level a building is to demolish it to the ground, which is what razing means.

clue.text: Op avoided by very good conductor, one of many on Broadway?

indicators.note: the two letters are shunned, so they are left out of the word that follows

blocks.note: taken as written; these letters are removed
top means excellent
a heater passes on heat, so in a sense conducts it

explanation.surface: An operation skipped by a fine orchestral conductor, one of many working on Broadway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Op' suggests a surgical or musical opus, but it is just two letters to strike from TOP. The American spelling suits Broadway.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadway in New York is lined with playhouses, spelt theater in American English.

clue.text: Group US lawsuit, Latin Sacco's undoing? (11, two words)

indicators.note: undoing something takes it apart, so the letters are pulled apart and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: The Italian anarchist Nicola Sacco's downfall in an American trial.
explanation.walkthrough: Sacco and Vanzetti were Italian immigrants executed in Massachusetts in 1927 after a notorious trial, which makes the surface fit a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A class action is a suit brought in US courts on behalf of a whole group of claimants together.

clue.text: Review magnetic field strength in unit of mass

blocks.note: a crit is a critique or review
H is the physics symbol for magnetic field strength

explanation.surface: A physics paper checking the strength of a magnetic field in some unit of mass.
explanation.definitionFit: A crith is the mass of a litre of hydrogen at standard conditions, an old unit for weighing gases.

clue.text: Something for WI vegetarians, semolina special twice demolished?

indicators.note: knocked out on two occasions means the letter goes from two places

blocks.note: couscous is made from semolina
S abbreviates special

explanation.surface: A Women's Institute vegetarian recipe built round semolina, with a special twist.
explanation.walkthrough: WI is the West Indies here, not the Women's Institute.
explanation.definitionFit: Coucou is a West Indian dish of cornmeal and okra, a meatless staple, so food for vegetarians there.

clue.text: Groom, conceited youngster taking in where curlers go? (7, two words)

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it within, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: a pup is an arrogant young man
curling is played on an ice rink

explanation.surface: A vain young man making himself smart, with hair curlers in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curlers' suggests hair rollers, but they are players of curling, the ice sport.
explanation.definitionFit: To prink up is to dress or preen oneself fussily, a sense of grooming oneself.

clue.text: Shared language certainly turning up among English

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: OK as an assent
in means among
E abbreviates English

explanation.surface: A common tongue is surely appearing among English speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: A koine is a common dialect used as a lingua franca, originally the Greek shared across the Hellenistic world.

clue.text: Grizzly's family usually found around river Shenandoah's source

indicators.note: the short word is wrapped around the letter that follows
the source of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: usu is the abbreviation for usually
R abbreviates river
first letter of the name

explanation.surface: Grizzly bears usually live near the source of the Shenandoah river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family' is loose: Ursus is the bear genus.
explanation.definitionFit: The grizzly belongs to Ursus, the Latin genus name of the true bears.

clue.text: Head in kitchen involved in ironing, thing abandoned for tea break?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
the word for an object is given up and taken out
involved means wrapped up within something else

blocks.note: first letter of the word
ironing smooths out creases
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: The chef gets caught up in ironing and abandons it for a cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: Smoko is Australian and New Zealand slang, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoko is an Australian and New Zealand word for a short work break, originally for a cigarette or cup of tea.

clue.text: The backward remain endlessly ignorant, as of old

indicators.note: without an end means the last letter is dropped
going backward means the word is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: to dwell is to stay or remain

explanation.surface: A disparaging remark that slow-witted people stay forever ignorant, as in former times.
explanation.walkthrough: The word's old sense was unlearned or lay, which is why 'as of old' is attached.
explanation.definitionFit: In archaic English lewd meant lay, unlearned or ignorant, long before it acquired its modern indecent sense.

clue.text: Although undamaged, centre surrendering place for international

indicators.note: giving up its position to another means one letter is swapped for a different one

blocks.note: whole means intact
the middle letter of that word
I abbreviates international

explanation.surface: Though unhurt, a central player gives way to an international.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre' and 'international' suggest a football team selection, but they are letter swaps.
explanation.definitionFit: While as a conjunction can mean although, as in 'while I agree, I have doubts'.

clue.text: Gordon's chicken or duck in casserole?

indicators.note: the round thing sits inside the cooking vessel

blocks.note: a casserole is a cooking pot
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Gordon asks whether chicken or duck is going in the casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gordon' is a stock Scots name, marking a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Poot is Scots for a young chicken or game bird, a poult.

clue.text: Dance music, vague noise in busy bar

indicators.note: a busy place is all bustle, so the letters are stirred around
the noise sits inside the jumbled word

blocks.note: a hum is an indistinct low sound
taken as written, then scrambled

explanation.surface: Music for dancing and a murmur of voices in a crowded bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhumba is a Cuban dance, and the name covers the music played for it as well.

clue.text: Reduce to smithereens book shortened in a volume

indicators.note: the book's name is cut to its short form before it goes in
the short book sits inside the phrase that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
a tome is a large book
Is is the standard abbreviation for the Book of Isaiah

explanation.surface: Tearing up a volume after one of its books has been abridged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortened' signals an abbreviation of a book of the Bible, not a cut word.
explanation.definitionFit: To atomise is to break something into tiny particles, just as smithereens are tiny fragments.

clue.text: Silly-billy, in other words 'nit'

blocks.note: a coot is a fool
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Calling someone a silly-billy is another way of calling them a nit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nit' looks like the insult nitwit, matching silly-billy, but it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Cootie is American slang for a louse, and a nit is a louse or its egg.

clue.text: Clipped opening of speech on the blower in LA?

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
one part comes next to the other, so they are joined in order

blocks.note: first letter of the word
in American slang the telephone is the horn, as the British say the blower

explanation.surface: Someone speaks curtly on the telephone in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The blower' is British slang for the telephone; in the US it is 'the horn'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorn is the past participle of shear, so it means cut or clipped, as a sheep's fleece is.

clue.text: Ninepins Scots scatter, first to last

indicators.note: the opening letter is moved round to the end of the word

blocks.note: skail is a Scots verb meaning to scatter or disperse

explanation.surface: Scots knock the skittles flying in a game of ninepins.
explanation.definitionFit: Kails is a Scots name for the game of ninepins or skittles, kail being one pin.

clue.text: For marriages I put in records on each occasion (13, two words)

indicators.note: the single letter is placed inside the following word

blocks.note: for and to are interchangeable in some uses, e.g. a toast for or to someone
a marriage is a tie between two people
taken as written
to quote is to cite or record

explanation.surface: A registrar logging weddings every time one takes place.
explanation.definitionFit: Toties quoties is Latin meaning as often as, used in English for each time or on every occasion.
